searched: I downloaded MidAmerican's Resource Evaluation Study of November 1, 2024 from the live address and read the preferred portfolio and action plan tables.

I read the Synapse Energy Economics comments of April 2025 on Interstate Power and Light's study, which is dated February 13, 2025 (docket RPU-2021-0003). I did not reach the study itself in the Iowa Utilities Commission filing system.

I read Alliant Energy's quarterly report for June 30, 2026 through the declared identity route. It lists Morgan Valley and Riverhawk as simple-cycle plants and mentions no combined cycle unit and no new Resource Evaluation Study.

A web search found no newer Resource Evaluation Study from Interstate Power and Light in 2025 or 2026, and none from MidAmerican since November 1, 2024. MidAmerican agreed to file an update within three years of its filing, so by November 1, 2027. I found no due date for Interstate Power and Light's next study. A Sierra Club report and the Office of Consumer Advocate suggest the commission has no rules yet for a study cycle.
I read the August 2026 EIA-860M table (Operating, Planned, Retired and Canceled sheets) for Iowa and checked every gas, oil and petroleum coke plant against GEM's list, including the coal tracker.
I read the full public interconnection queue of the Midcontinent Independent System Operator and listed every Iowa gas entry.
I read Cleanview's list of planned Iowa gas plants. Its entries are queue points, such as Killdeer, so I used the queue itself.

I searched the web for new gas plant proposals in Iowa in 2025 and 2026. I found only projects GEM already has (Orient, Bobcat, Cedar River, Burlington, Morgan Valley, Riverhawk, Hickory Grove) and the Muscatine turbine. I found no new cooperative or municipal proposal.

I could not search the Iowa Department of Natural Resources air construction permit notices. The page is a search form that needs a script. I also did not open the Iowa Utilities Commission filing system, so I did not list generating certificate dockets for 2025 and 2026 there.

I searched for data centers in Iowa with on-site gas. I found the Sailfish Council Bluffs campus and a temporary generator plan at the QTS campus in Cedar Rapids. I found no Google, Meta or Microsoft campus with on-site gas turbines.

The Sierra Club list's 'Alliant IA RES CC 2' of 1,720 MW: no primary source I read mentions a second Alliant combined cycle unit of that size. The Synapse comments mention only one 430 MW combined cycle unit, and Alliant's June 2026 report mentions none.
I did not run the entity lookup, because I named no new owner: every monitor item uses the owners named in the EIA table or leaves the owner open.

irp_summary.Interstate Power and Light Company: The February 2025 study modeled over 1,500 MW of new gas, including a 430 MW combined cycle unit in 2029, but I only reached comments on it and found no source that still lists that unit, so I raised the existing placeholder as a question and staged nothing new, and no due date for the next study was found.
irp_summary.MidAmerican Energy Company: The November 2024 study adds 3,495 MW of gas combustion turbines from 2028 to 2044, and Orient plus all seven placeholders match it, so nothing new was staged, and the study update is due by November 1, 2027.

qa.plant_name: Interstate Power and Light 2024 IRP power station 1
qa.recommendation: Keep the placeholder for now and ask the reviewer whether the 430 MW combined cycle unit is still planned. If not, the placeholder could be cancelled.
qa.note: This placeholder holds the 430 MW combined cycle unit for 2029 that Interstate Power and Light modeled in its Resource Evaluation Study. I could not read the study itself, because it is filed with the Iowa Utilities Commission in docket RPU-2021-0003 and I did not reach that filing system. Comments filed by Synapse Energy Economics on April 7, 2025 describe the study, which is dated February 13, 2025. They say the main flat load portfolio adds over 1,500 MW of new gas, made up of a 430 MW combined cycle unit and the rest peaking units. They also say the company expected combined cycle units to be available no earlier than 2029. Alliant Energy's quarterly report for June 30, 2026 lists only simple-cycle gas projects: about 720 MW in Linn County (Morgan Valley) and about 1,200 MW near Emery Station (Riverhawk). It does not mention a combined cycle unit at all. Bobcat (720 MW) is already tracked as its own plant. I found no source that says the 430 MW combined cycle unit was dropped or replaced, and none that says it is still planned. So the placeholder cannot be confirmed or removed on the evidence found. A reviewer should check the docket or ask Alliant.

qa.recommendation: No change needed. All seven MidAmerican placeholders match the plan. Optionally set this one to 233 MW to match the plan's rounded size.
qa.note: MidAmerican's Resource Evaluation Study of November 1, 2024 has a Preferred Portfolio table of gas combustion turbine additions. It lists 233 MW in 2028, 233 MW in 2029, 233 MW in 2031, 233 MW in 2033, 233 MW in 2035, 699 MW in 2041, 466 MW in 2042, 466 MW in 2043 and 699 MW in 2044, for a total of 3,495 MW. The 2028 and 2029 entries are the Orient Energy Center. The other seven are the placeholders: 233 MW in 2031 (this plant, which GEM holds at 232.5 MW), 233 MW in 2033, 233 MW in 2035, 699 MW in 2041, 466 MW in 2042, 466 MW in 2043 and 699 MW in 2044. Every year and size matches GEM, except that this plant is 232.5 MW in GEM and 233 MW in the plan. The plan models turbines in 233 MW blocks, and Orient's two turbines are each 232.5 MW, so the 0.5 MW gap is rounding. I read the table in the downloaded plan text.

qa.recommendation: Leave both units at 2028. The plan's 2029 entry for the second turbine is older than the company's own later statements.
qa.note: The tab note says MidAmerican plans two 233 MW peaking plants in 2028 and 2029, and GEM has both Orient units in 2028. MidAmerican's Resource Evaluation Study of November 1, 2024 does list one 233 MW turbine in 2028 and another in 2029. Its Action Plan table says the same, with a feasible timeline of 233 MW in each of those two years. A later MidAmerican news release says the Orient Energy Center, two gas-fired combustion turbines at one site in Adair County, will generate 465 MW beginning in 2028. The company gives no 2029 date for the second turbine in that release. A queue entry at the Midcontinent Independent System Operator for 263 MW at the Orient Energy Center substation, with service in November 2028, was withdrawn on December 23, 2025. A second entry for 263 MW at the Orient to Northboro line, with service in September 2027, is still active. I did not find which entry covers which turbine. I suggest keeping 2028 for both units unless the plant's own research finds a 2029 date.

qa.recommendation: Ask the reviewer to check whether Streeter Station was converted from coal to gas. If it was, add gas timepoint 2 units (16.5 MW and 35 MW) with Cedar Falls Utilities as owner.
qa.note: GEM has Streeter Station only in the coal tracker, as unit 7 (35 MW, 1973), retired. The EIA-860M table for August 2026 lists Streeter Station, plant 1131, owned by Cedar Falls Utilities in Black Hawk County. Both of its units are listed as natural gas steam turbines and as operating. Unit 6 is 16.5 MW from 1963. Unit 7 is 35 MW from 1973. That is 51.5 MW of gas capacity in total, which is over the 50 MW threshold. The EIA table does not say when the units switched from coal to gas. A September 2026 air permit application from Cedar Falls Utilities to the Iowa Department of Natural Resources says unit 6 now burns coal or natural gas, and asks to drop coal so that unit 6 becomes a gas-only boiler. It does not say whether unit 7 still runs. The owner name already exists in GEM as Cedar Falls Utilities.

monitor.plant_name: Sailfish Council Bluffs data center campus
monitor.monitor_reason: The developer says on-site gas will supply part of the power, but no gas generating capacity, permit or equipment has been named.
monitor.note: A Data Center Dynamics article on Sailfish Digital Ventures from 2025 says the company plans, in Council Bluffs, Iowa, a ten-building, 1 GW campus powered in part by on-site natural gas generation on a 306-acre site. The article is mainly about a Texas campus. A Council Bluffs paragraph sits in the same story, and the Sailfish chief executive says the company has partnered with a natural gas generation developer. I found no source that gives the gas capacity at Council Bluffs, the gas generation partner, a street address, an air permit, a generating certificate or a start of construction. The article says Sailfish had not yet delivered a data center, so the campus may not be funded. The 1 GW figure is the campus size, not the generating capacity. If it is added later, the captive fields would be captive industry use power and captive industry type data center. I searched for Council Bluffs gas generation for other developers too. The only other new Council Bluffs campus I found, Edged's two-building site, is reported at about 200 MW of load with no gas generation.
